title: Generation and application of TGFβ-educated human Vγ9Vδ2 T cells
author: Parente-Pereira, Beatson, et al.

steps.title: Coat plates with pan γδ TCR antibody
steps.instruction: On Day ‑1, coat 24‑, 12‑, or 6‑well plates (chosen based on expected PBMC number) overnight (12–16 h) at 4 °C with 0.8 mg/mL pan γδ TCR antibody (clone 11F2 or B1) diluted in PBS: use 1 mL per 24‑well, 2 mL per 12‑well, or 3 mL per 6‑well. CRITICAL: other pan γδ TCR antibodies have not been tested for activation.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs from donor blood
steps.instruction: On Day 0, collect ~45 mL peripheral blood from a consenting healthy donor into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 5 mL sodium citrate (or alternatively into sodium heparin tubes). Mix gently, then add an equal volume of PBS (1:1). Layer the blood/PBS mixture onto 15 mL Ficoll‑Paque Plus in the same tube using a gravity‑controlled pipette. Centrifuge at 750 × g for 30 min at 20 °C with acceleration and brake set to 0. Harvest the PBMC interface with a sterile Pasteur pipette, discard the plasma layer above if needed. Wash the PBMCs twice: first, add PBS to a final volume of 50 mL, centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min (acceleration/brake = 9.8); discard supernatant. If multiple tubes were used, combine pellets in TexMACS™ + medium, bring volume to 50 mL PBS for a second wash, centrifuge again at 500 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant. Resuspend the final pellet in TexMACS™ + medium (typically 10 mL per 45 mL blood). Count live cells with trypan blue and a hemocytometer (samples are usually diluted 1:10 with PBS) and adjust the suspension to 3 × 10⁶ cells/mL.

steps.title: Plate PBMCs and add activation reagents
steps.instruction: Immediately after isolation, plate the PBMCs at 3 × 10⁶ cells/mL in TexMACS™ + medium. Choose one of the following activation methods:

substeps.instruction: Antibody activation (for expanding both δ2 and non‑δ2 γδ T cells): Aspirate the antibody‑containing PBS from the coated plates (Step 1), wash each well once with PBS, then add 4 mL TexMACS™ + per well of a 6‑well plate. Add recombinant IL‑2 to a final concentration of 100 U/mL and recombinant TGF‑β1 to 5 ng/mL. After 72 h, harvest the cells from the plate.

Zoledronic acid activation (for expanding δ2 γδ T cells): Plate PBMCs at 3 × 10⁶ cells/mL in TexMACS™ + medium (no pre‑coating required). Add zoledronic acid to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL together with IL‑2 (100 U/mL) and TGF‑β1 (5 ng/mL).

steps.title: Culture cells with cytokine feeding
steps.instruction: From Day 1 to Day 14, monitor cell density by microscopy and counting every 2–3 days. Adjust cultures as follows:

substeps.instruction: If density > 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, add 100 % fresh TexMACS™ + medium together with IL‑2 (100 U/mL) and TGF‑β1 (5 ng/mL).
If density ≤ 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, add only IL‑2 (100 U/mL) and TGF‑β1 (5 ng/mL) to the existing volume (cytokine addition is corrected to the total volume present).
When necessary, split the cultures and expand into additional wells or T75 flasks to maintain optimal density.

steps.title: Assess γδ T‑cell purity by flow
steps.instruction: On Day 15, evaluate the proportion of γδ T cells by flow cytometry:

substeps.instruction: Transfer at least 5 × 10⁴ cells from each culture (γδ[2] and γδ[T2]) into separate 5 mL polystyrene tubes.
Wash each tube with 2 mL FACS buffer (PBS + 0.5 mM EDTA + 1 % FCS) and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 50 µL PBS.

Add 5 µL anti‑human γδ TCR‑FITC antibody (BD Biosciences, clone B1, Cat# 559878) to the tube containing γδ[2] cells and 5 µL FITC‑conjugated isotype control to the tube containing γδ[T2] cells (or vice‑versa, as long as each condition has a matched control).
Incubate both tubes on ice for 30 min.
Wash each tube again with 2 mL FACS buffer, centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100–250 µL PBS and acquire data on a flow cytometer.
PAUSE POINT: Cultures may be maintained up to Day 21 by continuing the feeding regimen described in Step 4.
